content: The text provided is a comprehensive and detailed list of treatment regimens for various bacterial infections, including specific dosages and administration routes for different patient populations. Treatment of Enterococcus faecalis Bacteremia 1. Ampicillin or Penicillin Susceptible Strains: Administer ampicillin 2 g intravenously (IV) every 4–6 hours, or combine ampicillin with gentamicin 1 mg/kg IV every 8 hours. 2. Ampicillin-Resistant and Vancomycin-Susceptible Strains or Penicillin Allergy: Use vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV every 12 hours in combination with gentamicin 1 mg/kg IV every 8 hours, or alternatively, administer linezolid 600 mg every 12 hours or daptomycin 6 mg/kg per day IV. 3. Ampicillin and Vancomycin-Resistant Strains: Administer linezolid 600 mg every 12 hours or daptomycin 6 mg/kg IV per day. Treatment of Enterococcus faecalis Endocarditis in Adults 1. Strains Susceptible to Penicillin, Gentamicin, and Vancomycin: Preferred regimen: Administer ampicillin 12 g/day IV for 4–6 weeks or aqueous crystalline penicillin G sodium 18–30 million units/day IV for 4–6 weeks, combined with gentamicin sulfate 3 mg/kg/day IV or intramuscularly (IM) for 4–6 weeks. Note: For native valve endocarditis, a 4-week therapy is recommended for patients with symptoms lasting ≤3 months, while a 6-week therapy is recommended for symptoms >3 months or in cases involving prosthetic valves or other prosthetic cardiac materials. 2. Alternate Regimen: Use vancomycin hydrochloride 30 mg/kg/day IV for 6 weeks combined with gentamicin sulfate 3 mg/kg/day IV or IM for 6 weeks. 3. Strains Susceptible to Penicillin, Streptomycin, and Vancomycin but Resistant to Gentamicin: Preferred regimen: Administer ampicillin 12 g/day IV for 4–6 weeks or aqueous crystalline penicillin G sodium 24 million units/day IV for 4–6 weeks, combined with streptomycin sulfate 15 mg/kg/day IV or IM for 4–6 weeks. 4. Alternate Regimen: Use vancomycin hydrochloride 30 mg/kg/day IV for 6 weeks combined with streptomycin sulfate 15 mg/kg/day IV or IM for 6 weeks. 5. Strains Resistant to Penicillin but Susceptible to Aminoglycosides and Vancomycin (β-Lactamase Producing Strains): Preferred regimen: Administer ampicillin-sulbactam 12 g/day IV for 6 weeks combined with gentamicin sulfate 3 mg/kg/day IV or IM for 6 weeks. 6. Intrinsic Penicillin Resistance: Use vancomycin hydrochloride 30 mg/kg/day IV for 6 weeks combined with gentamicin sulfate 3 mg/kg/day IV or IM for 6 weeks. 7. Strains Resistant to Penicillin, Aminoglycosides, and Vancomycin: Preferred regimen: Administer imipenem or cilastatin 2 g/day IV for ≥8 weeks combined with ampicillin 12 g/day IV for ≥8 weeks, or alternatively, use ceftriaxone sodium 4 g/day IV or IM for ≥8 weeks combined with ampicillin 12 g/day IV for ≥8 weeks. Treatment of Enterococcus faecalis Endocarditis in Pediatrics 1. Strains Susceptible to Penicillin, Gentamicin, and Vancomycin: Preferred regimen: Administer ampicillin 300 mg/kg/day IV for 4–6 weeks or penicillin 300,000 units/kg/day IV for 4–6 weeks, combined with gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV or IM for 4–6 weeks. Note: For native valve endocarditis, a 4-week therapy is recommended for symptoms lasting ≤3 months, while a 6-week therapy is recommended for symptoms >3 months or in cases involving prosthetic valves or other prosthetic cardiac materials. 2. Alternate Regimen: Use vancomycin 40 mg/kg/day IV for 6 weeks combined with gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV or IM for 6 weeks. 3. Strains Susceptible to Penicillin, Streptomycin, and Vancomycin but Resistant to Gentamicin: Preferred regimen: Administer ampicillin 300 mg/kg/day IV for 4–6 weeks or penicillin 300,000 units/kg/day IV for 4–6 weeks, combined with streptomycin 20–30 mg/kg/day IV or IM for 4–6 weeks. 4. Alternate Regimen: Use vancomycin hydrochloride 40 mg/kg/day IV for 6 weeks combined with streptomycin sulfate 15 mg/kg/day IV or IM for 6 weeks. 5. Strains Resistant to Penicillin but Susceptible to Aminoglycosides and Vancomycin (β-Lactamase Producing Strains): Preferred regimen: Administer ampicillin-sulbactam 300 mg/kg/day IV for 6 weeks combined with gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV or IM for 6 weeks. 6. Intrinsic Penicillin Resistance: Use vancomycin 40 mg/kg/day IV combined with gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV or IM for 6 weeks. 7. Strains Resistant to Penicillin, Aminoglycosides, and Vancomycin: Preferred regimen: Administer imipenem/cilastatin 60–100 mg/kg/day IV for ≥8 weeks combined with ampicillin 300 mg/kg/day IV for ≥8 weeks, or alternatively, use ceftriaxone 100 mg/kg/day IV or IM combined with ampicillin 300 mg/kg/day IV for ≥8 weeks. Treatment of Meningitis 1. Ampicillin-Susceptible Strains: Preferred regimen: Administer ampicillin 12 g/day IV every 4 hours combined with gentamicin 5 mg/kg/day IV every 8 hours. 2. Ampicillin-Resistant Strains: Preferred regimen: Use vancomycin 30–45 mg/kg/day IV every 8–12 hours combined with gentamicin 5 mg/kg/day IV every 8 hours. 3. Ampicillin and Vancomycin-Resistant Strains: Preferred regimen: Administer linezolid 600 mg IV every 12 hours.
